706258.t: Beekes derives it from Pre-Greek, based on its technical semantic domain and lack of resemblance to various Indo-European roots.

706201.t: According to Beekes, from the same Pre-Greek root as τέραμνον (téramnon, “chamber”).

706219.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʷʰéros, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷʰéros (“heat; warm weather”, from *gʷʰer- (“warm, hot”) + *-os (action noun suffix)).

706232.t: From some derivative of Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁- (“to do; to set”), and compared in particular to Sanskrit धाक (dhāká, “container”). See also τίθημι (títhēmi, “to place; to put”), from the same root.

706297.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dʰers-. Cognates include Sanskrit धृष्णोति (dhṛṣṇóti), Czech drzý and Lithuanian drąsus.

706243.t: From Proto-Hellenic *kʷʰḗr, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰwer-. Cognates include Latin ferus (“wild, savage”), and Old Church Slavonic звѣрь (zvěrĭ, “wild animal”).

706217.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *gʷʰer- Proto-Indo-European *-mos Proto-Indo-European *gʷʰermos Proto-Hellenic *kʷʰermós Ancient Greek θερμός From Proto-Hellenic *kʷʰermós, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷʰer-mo-s (“warm”), from the root *gʷʰer-.

706223.t: Directly from τίθημι (títhēmi, “to put, place”) + -σις (-sis). Although, it could either have been formed in Greek, or Proto-Indo-European.

706229.t: From an earlier *θεα-(ϝ)ορός (*theā-(w)orós), *θεη-(ϝ)ορός (*theē-(w)orós), from the roots of θέα (théā, “sight, view, perspective”) + ὁράω (horáō, “I see”), i.e. "(of one who) watches a show".

706224.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dʰh₁-dʰmó-s, from *dʰeh₁- (“to do, put, place”). Cognate with Welsh deddf (“act, statute”).

706244.t: Back-formation from θηράω (thēráō, “to hunt”). Compare Tocharian B śerwe (“hunter”).

706293.t: A formation like ὄτοβος (ótobos), κόναβος (kónabos) and φλοῖσβος (phloîsbos), likely from the same root as a reduplicated form τονθορύζω (tonthorúzō, “to mumble”), as well as θρῦλος (thrûlos, “murmur”).

706260.t: Formation like θύρσος (thúrsos). An expression of the Dionysiac religion, and as such suspected of foreign origin: probably Pre-Greek, in spite of older interpretations in Indo-European terms.

706272.t: From θλάω (thláō, “I crush, I bruise”) and the suffix -μα (-ma).

706269.t: Due to the improbability of the other explanations, Beekes suggests a Pre-Greek origin.

706261.t: A loan from Semitic. Compare Hebrew תֵּבָה (tēḇā, “ark, vessel”), Arabic تَابُوت (tābūt).

706274.t: Unknown. It has been proposed to be a blend between θλάω (thláō, “to crush, bruise”) and φλίβω (phlíbō, “to squeeze”).

706262.t: Perhaps inherited from Proto-Indo-European *dʰi-né-ǵʰ-ti ~ *dʰi-n-ǵʰ-énti, a nasal-infix present from *dʰeyǵʰ- (“to mold”), with supposed parallels in Latin fingō (“to shape; feign”) and Old Armenian դիզանեմ (dizanem, “to heap up, gather”).

706273.t: Unknown, though note also θλίβω (thlíbō, “to squeeze, distress”) and φλάω (phláō, “to crush, bruise”). Not related to θλάσπις (thlắspĭs, “shepherd's purse”), despite folk etymological linkage.
